heroHeadline: Day 379: Back-Channel Meetings Revealed — Four Quiet India-Pakistan Contacts Since Ceasefire as Airspace Freeze Deepens
heroSubtitle: May 24, 2026: Al Jazeera (May 23) reveals four informal back-channel meetings between Indian and Pakistani officials and former officials have been held since the May 10, 2025 ceasefire — in Muscat, Doha, Bangkok, and London — the most concrete evidence yet of quiet India-Pakistan contact. Pakistan's FM declined to confirm, saying 'If I was to comment, there would be no back channel.' India's airspace NOTAM on Pakistani aircraft reached its May 24 expiry; Pakistan's symmetric ban on Indian aircraft runs through June 23/24. The IWT legal dispute remains live: Pakistan's Foreign Office (May 23) reaffirmed its position after India's May 16 rejection of the PCA's May 15 supplemental award as 'null and void.' All other bilateral mechanisms remain severed: $0 formal trade, no ambassadors, no official dialogue. The ceasefire continues to hold at Day 379 with no LOC incidents.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
